meth.coef.age: Building age uses the obsolescence table of the IMI (property tax) code (from 1.00 for under 2 years to 0.40 over 60 years), normalised to "9 to 15 years".

meth.draft: Draft: figures to be confirmed at implementation. Model v0.2 · revised 28/10/2026.
meth.ex.note: The thresholds are inspired by German rules (10%, 20% and 50%). In Portugal they are not legal limits.
meth.ex.title: How we read the excess
meth.how.s1.n: INE area median ÷ 1.30 (estimated overvaluation between 20% and 35%)
meth.how.s2.n: what a couple on two median incomes pays at 30% effort, 3% interest, 30 years and 90% financing
meth.how.s3.n: average of the two anchors, with a range between 30/70 and 70/30
meth.how.title: How we reach the reference price
meth.hyp.body: There is no official source for these points. They are our choices, flagged as such and open to review.
meth.hyp.title: Project assumptions
meth.layers.effort: Effort: arithmetic on official data. How much of the payment or rent is taken from net income, compared with 30% (reference) and 45% (Banco de Portugal cap since 1 August 2026, with interest +1.5 p.p.).
meth.layers.ref: Reference price: a model with two anchors, the market corrected for overvaluation and what local income can pay, adjusted for the property's condition, age and features.
meth.layers.title: Two layers of result
meth.lim.1: Areas with few transactions appear as "Insufficient data".
meth.lim.2: Median values do not distinguish view, floor or sun exposure.
meth.lim.3: Income data lag by one or more years; we update them with wage growth.
meth.lim.4: A price above the reference does not prove abuse: it shows the distance from what local income supports.
meth.lim.title: Limitations
meth.read.excess: Excess: how far the price is above the reference. On the map it compares the area’s market median with the reference price; in the calculator it compares the listing price with the property’s reference. It is not compared with salary: income only enters inside the reference, in anchor S2.
meth.read.market: Market median: the price per m² INE records for sales in the area (median of the last 12 months). It is what is asked and paid today.
meth.read.reference: Reference price: the price per m² the model considers reasonable for the area. It is the average of two anchors: the market corrected for overvaluation (S1) and what local income can pay (S2).
meth.read.title: How to read the numbers
meth.sigma.bdp: Banco de Portugal: price-to-income above its long-run average (end of 2024)
meth.sigma.chosen: We chose 30%, between 20% and 35%, and always show the reference with both ends. It is a project assumption: the estimates measure different things, at different dates, and none is by municipality.
meth.sigma.limits: Limits: it is national (Lisbon and the interior get the same correction); it only affects half of the reference (anchor S1); and it can be changed under “Your parameters”.
meth.sigma.title: Overvaluation correction (σ)
meth.sigma.what: σ is our estimate of how far the market is above what economic fundamentals, mainly incomes, justify. We use 30%: anchor S1 is the median ÷ 1.30. It does not measure speculation or anyone’s intentions: it is a statistical correction, the same for the whole country.
meth.src.at: Tax Authority: IMI code (obsolescence, construction value).
meth.src.bdp: Banco de Portugal: effort cap (45%), financial stability.
meth.src.eu: European Commission and IMF: overvaluation estimates.
meth.src.ine: INE: prices, rents and income by municipality.
meth.src.rent: Portaria 454/2026/1: maximum rents under the Affordable Rent scheme.

meth.title: Methodology and sources
meth.what.body: The reference price measures what local income supports, adjusted for the property's condition. It does not measure what the market accepts: it ignores demand on purpose. The market median (factual) always appears alongside our reference price (normative).
